faq.answer: Revisit it when an update, new pet, different variant, or changed goal affects your next choice. Start by checking the entries you are actively comparing.

faq.question: Where can I compare income values?
faq.answer: Open the Value List for the public Cat and Geek Cat figures, then compare the current individual income shown for your own pets using the same unit.

faq.question: Are these official S–D game ranks?
faq.answer: The S–D labels are editorial. The official artwork supplies the animal names, Common and Divine rarity labels, and displayed incomes; the tier labels help organize your priorities.

sections.heading: Steal Animal Egg Value List
paragraphs: These are public income reference points from official Roblox artwork, rather than a complete live roster. Your exact variant may show different information in game. Both figures use /s, presenting a per-second earning comparison.

Geek Cat has the higher printed income in this pair. The Q abbreviation is retained exactly as it appears in the image. For a decision in your current collection, compare the live value attached to each actual pet or variant you own.

sections.heading: What “Value” Means Here
paragraphs: This Steal Animal Egg value list focuses on displayed pet income and practical progression rather than speculative trade-price estimates. Income answers how the pet contributes to earnings. Progression context helps when you are choosing what to pursue next instead of comparing pets already in your collection.

A collection preference is useful too, but it answers a different question. You may want a particular name or appearance even when another entry earns more. Keep that preference separate from the numerical comparison so each decision is easy to explain.

sections.heading: How to Compare Pet Income
paragraphs: Choose the two or more pets relevant to your current goal. Read their individual earning information under similar conditions, then follow this short comparison. A collection total describes the group, while an individual figure lets you order specific pets.

steps.heading: Read the exact pet and variant name
steps.description: Keep the full name and any visible size or mutation label together. Cat and Geek Cat are distinct public names, and different variants in your collection deserve separate entries.

steps.heading: Match the unit and time basis
steps.description: Compare per-second income with per-second income, or another matching unit shown by the game. Keep the unit with the figure so the two entries measure the same thing.

steps.heading: Use the current displayed value
steps.description: Read the number for the pet in your session and compare the matching figures. Recheck both entries when a new variant or an update changes the choice.

subsections.heading: Choosing between owned pets and a target
paragraphs: For pets you already own, the current comparable income is directly relevant. A future target also needs a practical acquisition plan. Keep the value comparison available, then use the tier guide to decide whether the target is the right next priority.

sections.heading: Income vs Rarity, Size and Mutation
paragraphs: Income is the earning figure; rarity is the displayed classification. In the official examples, Cat is Common and Geek Cat is Divine. Those labels help identify the entries, while the attached income is the number used for the earning comparison.

Size and mutation are part of the game’s highlighted egg details. Keep them with the exact pet name when the interface shows them. For a mutated pet, use the value displayed for that variant in your current session. That gives you a comparison tied to the pet you can actually use.

sections.heading: Tier List vs Value List
paragraphs: The value list supplies numbers and their context; the tier list supplies priorities. Higher current income is a strong signal for an earning goal, while a reliable next acquisition helps you turn the comparison into an action you can complete.

The animal reference is a useful starting point when a name is unfamiliar. Identify the pet first, compare its earnings next, and choose its priority afterward. This keeps the three pages focused on different parts of a collection decision instead of repeating the same answer.

sections.heading: Value List Updates
paragraphs: After a game update or a new hatch, revisit the pets that affect your next choice. Compare both entries using current information and keep older observations separate. The Last updated date helps you recognize the web reference, while the live pet information keeps the decision current.

Code rewards can also relate to income. ENDGAME and DEMONIC are listed as ten-minute income rewards. Their reward descriptions measure a period of income, so read the redemption response separately from an individual pet’s earning figure. The code page keeps current rewards and expired entries together.

faq.question: What is the most valuable animal in Steal Animal Egg?
faq.answer: Geek Cat has the higher displayed income of the two official public examples on this page. For your collection, compare the current earning figure of each exact variant using the same unit.

faq.question: Is value the same as rarity?
faq.answer: No. Rarity identifies a classification such as Common or Divine in the public examples. Value here is the displayed earning figure and the progression context for your choice.

faq.question: Does size determine value?
faq.answer: Use the current income shown for the actual pet, with any size information kept alongside it. The earning figure gives you a direct comparison for that entry.

faq.question: Do mutations affect value?
faq.answer: Read the income displayed for the exact mutated variant in your session. Keep its mutation label with the name when comparing it with another pet.

faq.question: Is this a trading value list?
faq.answer: This is an income and progression reference rather than a community trade-price list. The numbers in the table come from official promotional artwork, and current pet income belongs to the live game display.

faq.question: Can I compare code income rewards with pet values?
faq.answer: Treat them as different measures. ENDGAME and DEMONIC grant rewards described as minutes of income, while the pet values shown here are printed per second. Read the reward response and the relevant live earning label.
